tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...', 'Do not use for...'), focuses on user intent (what questions the user asks, what scenarios trigger the skill), and explicitly enumerates many trigger contexts (audit coverage, specific resource checks, organization trail questions, pasted trail output) as well as explicit exclusions (cost questions, who-performed-action, CIS scoring, making changes). While it is lengthy, the length is justified by the breadth of trigger/exclusion scenarios needed to correctly route this skill versus adjacent skills (cost-optimization, Security Hub), and it remains a single coherent paragraph without describing internal implementation mechanics.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when a user asks to audit or review CloudTrail coverage or configuration... Do not use for CloudTrail cost, bill, duplicate trail waste or data event charge questions, for finding who performed an action or searching logged events, for CIS or Security Hub control scoring, or to change any trail or selector."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and domain-specific throughout — it never explains what CloudTrail, S3, or Lambda are in general terms. Every sentence conveys a non-obvious rule (full ARN requirement, shadow trails, coverage states) specific to this skill's domain, with no generic filler.
tests.evidence: "Organization trails by full ARN, always. A failed name call is a mistake to retry, never a permission boundary."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed tables (API call fields, full check matrix details, permissions) are offloaded to references/ files and loaded conditionally at specific steps. The body only lists summarized check names and short selector semantics needed to understand the flow, not full lookup tables.
tests.evidence: "Full rules, selector semantics and worked examples: [coverage-model.md](references/coverage-model.md), loaded at Step 6."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five reference files are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies exactly when to load it (step number or trigger condition like AccessDenied).
tests.evidence: "Action table and denied call handling: [permissions.md](references/permissions.md), loaded on `AccessDenied`."

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consistency-critical operations (full ARN calls, 20-check matrix, rating roll-up) are given exact prescriptive rules, while scope resolution and mapping explain rationale (why ARN vs name) rather than being purely rigid, appropriately calibrated to fragility.
tests.evidence: "Call GetTrail, GetTrailStatus, GetEventSelectors and GetInsightSelectors with the full TrailARN, never the name; a name call returns TrailNotFoundException and proves nothing."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present a menu of competing tools/approaches for the same task; it specifies the exact API calls to use as the canonical procedure, with no alternate options listed as equal choices.
tests.evidence: "ListTrails, then DescribeTrails per enabled Region with shadow trails included; de duplicate by TrailARN."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable 9-step procedure (resolve scope, inventory, selectors, map, render) that applies to any account/prompt, not a one-off instance; specific details like templates and check lists are embedded within that generalizable approach.
tests.evidence: "Run every step on every run, however narrow the prompt."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A dedicated 'Known Quirks' section documents concrete, non-obvious environment facts (Event history limits, multipart upload event names, shadow trail dedup) that the agent would otherwise miss.
tests.evidence: "S3 multipart uploads emit CreateMultipartUpload, UploadPart, CompleteMultipartUpload, not PutObject; bulk deletes emit DeleteObjects."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a structured report and explicitly provides a template reference file for it.
tests.evidence: "The final message to the user is the full report defined in [report-template.md](references/report-template.md)"

tests.evidence: "Render from [report-template.md](references/report-template.md) at Step 9: one Trail Inventory row per unique trail and store..."
